item.title: Assignments
item.description: Assignments Every project and reading is fully specified at the bottom of the lecture where it’s introduced. This page is the index.

item.title: A Theory of Fun
item.description: Raph Koster (A Theory of Fun for Game Design): “fun” is a particular kind of pattern recognition that humans have evolved to be good at and feel rewarded for engaging in.

item.title: Affordances of Movement
item.description: How it feels to traverse the world.

item.title: Agency and Self-Efficacy
item.description: The feeling that you have the capability to effect change — the belief that what you do matters.

item.title: Alice in Wonderland as Game Precursor
item.description: A scene from Alice in Wonderland: a high table, a bottle labeled “Drink me,” a key, a door too small to fit through. At first look it’s nonsense.

item.title: Anticipation in Games
item.description: Several distinct mechanisms create anticipation in games: Dramatic situations.

item.title: Asset Reuse for Illusion of Variety
item.description: The whole forest in Firewatch — a game that’s largely about walking through a forest — uses only 23 tree models.

item.title: Character Dilemmas
item.description: When it isn’t the player who is faced with a dilemma, but a character — that’s a story. Dilemmas put characters under pressure.

item.title: Choices — Risk Reward, Builds, Progression, Emotional Weight
item.description: Four common shapes for meaningful choice in games: Risk and reward — two paths of unequal challenge and outcome.

item.title: Collaborative Playtesting
item.description: Sometimes it’s useful to have two playtesters, even when the game is a single-player experience.
